answer: A swarm of fresh wallets tries to fake a merchant guild into extending credit. The guild’s ledger ignores new names and instead weights each agent’s history as a slowly grown glacier of verified trades—never bought, only accumulated across time. Reputation melts when idle, so dormant sock puppets lose their mass before the next raid, while active traders keep a steady core. Every claim must be backed by a continuous ember trail of small settled transactions, and any suspicious identity needs a fable corroborated by long-standing peers before it can borrow trust.
